decisions.reason: A complete same-message MODIFY already limits dashboard rendering to NFTs from the active replacement contract and excludes legacy-contract NFTs.
A complete same-message MODIFY already limits owner discovery to replacement-contract NFTs and marks legacy-contract NFTs as undiscoverable.
A complete same-message MODIFY already excludes legacy-contract NFTs from active ownership and mint reporting.
A same-message MODIFY already records that future Transak mints target only the active replacement contract; no existing attribute became obsolete.
A same-message MODIFY already scopes unlimited NFT minting to the active replacement contract without changing the asset format or unlimited supply.
A same-message MODIFY already scopes USDC wallet mints to the active replacement contract; the payment asset and required mint behavior remain unchanged.
The migration policy is already established by an event from the source message with message 538 as supporting context, so no additional propagated MODIFY is needed.
Excluding old-contract NFTs from the active system does not change the royalty amount, enforcement standard, marketplace policy, or pool-funding behavior.
The migration decision does not alter how book access, referral identity, badges, or prize-ticket state follow an NFT when it is transferred.
Replacing the contract and excluding legacy NFTs does not change the required Base network deployment.
Fresh replacement-contract NFTs still use their token serials as permanent referral codes; the source does not change referral identity or display locations.
The contract-migration data policy does not require a change to the supplied About-page content or its current prize-mechanics copy.
